prompt: Lee gets {m:1500} and wants {m:900} to stay in Spend. Set the split.
wrong: Not quite. Spend should show {m:900}. Save gets the rest.
hints: Look at the Spend number as you slide.
Spend and Save make {m:1500}. If Spend is {m:900}, what's left for Save?
correct: Nice. That's it. {m:900} in Spend and {m:600} in Save make {m:1500}.

prompt: Remi's allowance is {m:1800}. Remi keeps {m:1100} for Spend. How much goes to Save?

misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. That adds the two. Spend is part of the {m:1800}, so take it away.
Not quite. That's the Spend part. What's left for Save?

wrong: Not quite. Save gets whatever doesn't go to Spend.
hints: Spend and Save together make {m:1800}.
{m:1800} take away {m:1100}.
correct: That's it. {m:700} goes to Save, and {m:1100} plus {m:700} makes {m:1800}.

prompt: Ari gets {m:2000}. Split it so at least {m:1200} stays in Spend for a trip, and some goes to Save.
wrong: Not quite. Check that Spend has at least {m:1200} and Save isn't empty.
hints: Watch the Spend number as you slide.
If Save goes above {m:800}, Spend drops below {m:1200}.
correct: Nice. That's it. Spend covers the trip, and the rest is in Save.

prompt: Jo takes {m:400} out of Save and puts it in Spend. Does Jo have more money in total now?

options.feedback: Not quite. Spend goes up, but Save goes down by the same amount.

options.text: No, the total is the same

options.feedback: Not quite. Nothing leaves Jo's jars. It just moves from one to the other.

outcome: Save goes down by {m:400} and Spend goes up by {m:400}. Jo's total stays the same. Moving money between jars is never new money.
hints: Look at both jars.
One jar goes up by {m:400}. What happens to the other?
correct: Right. The total is the same. The money just moved.

prompt: Noor plans {m:350} for Save and {m:550} for Spend from a {m:1000} allowance. What's off about this plan?

options.feedback: Yes. {m:350} and {m:550} make {m:900}, so {m:100} is missing.
Not quite. How much to save is Noor's choice. Check that the parts add up.
Not quite. Add {m:350} and {m:550}, then compare with {m:1000}.

hints: Add the two parts together.
correct: Nice. That's it. The parts must add up to the whole, so {m:100} still needs a jar.

prompt: Sam gets {m:1800}. Save exactly a third and keep the rest in Spend.
wrong: Not quite. A third is one of three equal parts. Save gets one part.
hints: Split {m:1800} into three equal parts.
Three lots of what make {m:1800}? Try {m:500}, then go up.
correct: Nice. That's it. A third of {m:1800} is {m:600}, so {m:1200} is for Spend.

prompt: Kai saves a tenth of a {m:3000} birthday gift. How much goes to Save?

misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. That's a third. A tenth means ten equal parts.
Not quite. That's what's left for Spend. Save gets the tenth.

wrong: Not quite. Split {m:3000} into ten equal parts. Save gets one.
hints: A tenth means ten equal parts.
Ten lots of what make {m:3000}?
correct: That's it. A tenth of {m:3000} is {m:300}.

prompt: Which of these saves exactly half of the allowance?
hints: Half means the Save part, doubled, makes the whole allowance.
Double each Save amount. Which one matches its allowance?

prompt: Remi always saves a quarter. Remi's allowance goes up from {m:800} to {m:1200}. What happens to the Save part?

options.feedback: Not quite. A share changes when the whole changes. Find a quarter of {m:1200}.
Not quite. That's the whole rise. Only a quarter of it goes to Save.

outcome: A quarter of {m:800} is {m:200}. A quarter of {m:1200} is {m:300}. Saving a share means your saving grows when your allowance does.
hints: Work out a quarter of each allowance.
A quarter of {m:800} is {m:200}. Now try {m:1200}.
correct: Right. The Save part goes from {m:200} to {m:300}.

prompt: Why might someone save a share, like a quarter, instead of a set amount each time?

options.text: Their saving grows when their allowance grows
A share is always more money
options.feedback: Not quite. A share can be more or less than a set amount. It moves with the allowance.

options.text: With a share you never need to plan
options.feedback: Not quite. You still choose the share. It just keeps working when the allowance changes.

hints: What happens to a quarter when the allowance goes up?
A set amount stays put. A share moves with the allowance.
correct: Right. A share keeps the same balance between Spend and Save, whatever you get.
